ai.description: This medium-sized frog reaches 40–50 mm. It is brown with dark dorsal mottling and prominent, glandular skin ridges. Distinctive features include a white upper lip stripe and heavily webbed toes.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Odorrana mawphlangensis* is best distinguished by the presence of a distinct, white, glandular fold extending from behind the eye to the shoulder, lacking in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Mawphlang Wart Frog inhabits subtropical evergreen forests and rocky stream banks in the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, typically at altitudes between 1,000 and 1,800 meters.
ai.behavior: The Mawphlang Wart Frog is primarily nocturnal, emerging at night to forage for small invertebrates along the rocky, fast-flowing streams of its forest habitat.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Odorrana mawphlangensis* is an oviparous frog that breeds during the monsoon season (June–August), depositing eggs in small, gelatinous clutches within rocky stream pools.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Mawphlang Wart Frog is endemic to the Khasi Hills of Meghalaya, India, typically inhabiting forest streams at elevations between 1,000 and 1,500 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Mawphlang Wart Frog produces a high-pitched, rhythmic series of short, metallic chirps while calling from rocky, fast-flowing streams in forested habitats.
